turns.doctor_question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, good to meet you too, Doc. I guess... well, what finally got me in here is that over these past few months, things have just been a little out of hand with my focus. I've been driving a truck for a long time, right? Straight out of high school, basically. And I'm a sharp guy, I know my routes, I know my clients, I know how to run my schedule tight. But lately, my mind just keeps jumping all over the place. I mean, it's like a pinball machine up there. 

Every single time the CB radio chirps—and you know those things are always going off with some guy complaining about a weigh station or traffic or whatever—or even just driving past a fuel price sign on the interstate... I mean, diesel prices are all over the place right now, but I'll see a sign and suddenly my brain is completely derailed, or I'll get this brand new idea out of nowhere about how to reorganize my routes or start a side business, and I just run with it in my head for miles. 

And the real problem with all that jumping around is that I'm missing details. Details I normally never, ever miss. Like, just the other day I completely missed a client’s delivery note about their loading dock hours changing, which was a whole mess to sort out, or I'll realize hours later that I completely forgot who I promised to call back from dispatch. It's just frustrating because usually I'm the guy who remembers everything, every name, every dock number, but lately it's just... chirp, sign, new idea, and the actual important stuff just vanishes on me.

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient explicitly states they are missing details they normally never miss, such as a client's delivery note.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient describes being easily distracted by extraneous stimuli like CB radio chirps and fuel price signs.
symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient mentions forgetting daily activities, such as who they promised to call back from dispatch.
symptom_reasoning.S038: The patient describes their mind jumping around 'like a pinball machine' and getting new ideas out of nowhere that they run with in their head.
symptom_reasoning.S039: The patient's attention is easily drawn to irrelevant external stimuli (CB chirps, fuel signs) and unrelated new ideas, derailing their train of thought.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been needing less sleep than usual and still feeling full of energy?
turns.patient_response:
Well, it's funny you ask that, because sleep has been a whole different ballgame lately. Normally, you know, you drive a rig for ten, eleven hours a day, staring at those white lines, dealing with four-wheelers cutting you off—by the time you shut down for the night, you are just dead to the world. You need that solid seven or eight hours just to function and keep it between the ditches. 

But lately? Man, I don't know what's gotten into me. Most nights I sleep maybe three or four hours, tops. And the weirdest part is, I don't feel tired at all. I'll wake up way before daylight, like 2:30 or 3:00 in the morning, and I am just wide awake, feeling ready to roll instead of worn out. I mean, not even a single yawn. I'll just pop right up out of the bunk, make a pot of coffee that I don't even really need, and start wiping down the cab, checking my gauges, going over my manifests again and again... just pacing around waiting for the sun to come up so I can get moving. 

If I'm actually at home and not on the road, my wife thinks I'm absolutely nuts because I'll be out in the driveway reorganizing my truck's toolbox in the pitch black. You'd think living on three hours of sleep I'd be dragging my feet or needing a nap by noon, but no, I just keep on going with a full tank of gas, so to speak. It's actually kind of nice for getting a head start on the morning weigh station lines, but I know it ain't exactly normal for me to run on so little rest and still feel this... I don't know, this charged up.

symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient describes feeling 'charged up' and running on a 'full tank of gas' with abnormally increased energy.
symptom_reasoning.S036: The patient explicitly states they sleep only three or four hours a night but wake up feeling 'ready to roll' and not tired at all.
symptom_reasoning.S040: The patient describes an increase in goal-directed activities, such as reorganizing their truck's toolbox in the pitch black and repeatedly checking manifests.

turns.doctor_question: During these past few months, have you been feeling unusually euphoric or on top of the world?
turns.patient_response:
Well, yeah, actually. It’s been… it’s been a really strange mix, to be honest with you. For months now, I’ve had these stretches where I just feel absolutely unstoppable. I mean, fired up in a way I haven't felt since I was in my twenties, maybe even better than that. It’s like this feeling in my chest that everything is just going to work out perfectly, no matter what I do. I’ll be cruising down the highway and I’ll just think, "Man, I could buy my own fleet. I could run this whole logistics game." It’s this massive confidence, like I’m on top of the world and nothing can touch me, not dispatch, not the DOT, nobody. 

But then, on the flip side of that same coin, and this is what’s really been bothering my wife, I get so... irritable. Just snapping over the smallest, dumbest things. Like, I’ll be home on a Saturday, trying to get some yard work done, and if the weed whacker string gets tangled, or if the dog barks at the mailman at the wrong time, I just explode. I mean, I’m yelling, I’m throwing tools in the yard. And that’s just not me, Doc. I’m usually a pretty easygoing guy, you know? You have to be, to drive a truck for thirty years. You learn to roll with the punches. But lately, it’s either I’m king of the road and every idea I have is pure gold, or I’m biting someone’s head off because they looked at me funny at the truck stop diner. It’s just this constant extreme, either way too high up or just completely ticked off at the world, and it’s been going on for months like this.

symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient describes feeling 'unstoppable' and 'on top of the world,' alternating with periods of being highly irritable and 'ticked off at the world.'
symptom_reasoning.S035: The patient expresses massive confidence and grandiosity, believing they could buy their own fleet and that every idea they have is 'pure gold.'
symptom_reasoning.S060: The patient reports snapping over minor stimuli, such as a tangled weed whacker string or a dog barking.
symptom_reasoning.S077: The patient describes angry outbursts involving verbal and physical aggression, such as yelling and throwing tools in the yard.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been taking on a lot more projects or activities than usual lately?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, man, you have no idea. It’s like I can’t even sit down for five minutes without finding something else that needs doing. Normally, you know, a guy my age, you get home from a long haul on a Friday, you want to grab a cold beer, sink into the recliner, and just watch the game. But not me. Not lately. I just keep finding extra jobs for myself, constantly, like I'm on some kind of mission. 

Take my routes, for example. I’ve been staying up and completely rewriting all my route plans. And I don't mean just glancing at the GPS—I mean getting out the physical maps, cross-referencing the construction schedules, trying to shave off two miles here or avoid a tricky intersection there, recalculating all my fuel stops to save a couple of pennies a gallon... it’s a whole massive production. And then, even when I’m strictly off the clock, I’m calling up the new guys at the company. I'll just be checking on the new drivers after hours, calling them at 8 or 9 PM when I really should be winding down. I just feel like I have to make sure they know how to handle the steep grades, or asking if they actually manually checked their tire pressure, because these kids today just rely on dashboard sensors, you know? 

And if I’m not doing truck stuff, I’m tearing through the house. I fixed the loose floorboards on the back porch that have been sitting there for three years, I repainted the trim in the garage, I even started taking apart the lawnmower engine on a Tuesday night just to see if I could get it running a little smoother. My wife is looking at me like I’ve got two heads because I just can’t stop. If I try to force myself to just sit on the couch and watch a show with her, my leg starts bouncing, I get all jittery... I just feel completely antsy if I sit still for too long. I have to be moving, I have to be fixing something or planning something, or I just feel like I'm gonna crawl right out of my own skin. It's just go, go, go, all the time.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient explicitly states feeling 'completely antsy if I sit still for too long' and feeling like they will 'crawl right out of my own skin'.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient describes being constantly in motion, stating 'It's just go, go, go, all the time' and being unable to sit down for five minutes.
symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient confirms taking on numerous extra projects, such as rewriting route plans, checking on drivers, and doing home repairs, indicating abnormally increased activity and energy.
symptom_reasoning.S040: The patient details a significant increase in goal-directed activities both related to work (route planning, calling drivers) and at home (fixing floorboards, painting, repairing a lawnmower).
symptom_reasoning.S058: The patient describes feeling 'antsy' and 'all jittery' when attempting to relax, indicating physical tension and restlessness.

turns.doctor_question: During these past few months, have you been acting noticeably unlike your usual self?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I guess... I mean, "unlike my usual self" is a funny way to put it, because I still feel like me, you know? Just... maybe a louder, faster version of me. But if you ask my wife, or some of the guys at the depot, they might say something different. Like, I’ve been driving a truck for thirty years, right? You get a reputation for being steady. Reliable. You don't make waves, you just get the freight from point A to point B. 

But lately... I don't know, I haven't really noticed myself acting all that crazy or anything. I mean, sure, I'm doing more, like I said with the projects and the routes and all that, and I'm a little more irritable, but I wouldn't say I'm some completely different person. I'm just getting things done. But then again, my dispatcher did pull me aside the other day and asked if I was drinking too much coffee, which is ridiculous because I always drink the same amount of coffee, but he said I was talking so fast on the radio he couldn't understand me. And I guess I have been a little more... forward, maybe? Like, usually I just nod and take my paperwork, but last week I spent twenty minutes lecturing the shipping clerk about how inefficient their loading dock schedule is, and I drew up a whole diagram on the back of a manifest to show him how to fix it. He just looked at me like I was from Mars. 

So, I don't know if I'd say I'm noticeably unlike my usual self, because to me, it just makes sense in the moment. I'm just trying to improve things, you know? But I suppose other people are looking at me a little sideways. Does that make sense? I mean, what do you even consider "usual" when things are just running so much faster than they normally do?

symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient explicitly states that he has been 'a little more irritable' lately.
symptom_reasoning.S037: The patient reports that his dispatcher said he was talking so fast on the radio he couldn't be understood, and he spent 20 minutes lecturing a clerk.
symptom_reasoning.S040: The patient describes doing more with projects and routes, and engaging in new goal-directed tasks like drawing up an efficiency diagram for a shipping clerk.

turns.doctor_question: During these high-energy periods, have you had experiences like hearing or seeing things other people don’t, or being certain you had special powers or an extraordinary mission?
turns.patient_response:
Hearing or seeing things? No, no, definitely not. I mean, let's be real here, if I was seeing things that weren't on the road, I'd have handed over my CDL a long time ago. You can't be hauling eighty thousand pounds of freight down a steep grade in the rain if your eyes are playing tricks on you. The DOT doesn't mess around with that, and neither do I. I’ve passed every physical they’ve thrown at me since nineteen ninety-four. My vision is sharp, my hearing is fine... well, maybe a little ringing in the left ear from having the window cracked for thirty years, but I'm definitely not hearing voices or anything spooky like that. 

And as for special powers or some kind of secret mission? Nah, nothing crazy like that. I mean, I told you earlier that I feel like I could run the whole logistics company, but that’s not because I think I'm Superman or something. It’s just because I’ve been doing this for three decades and I actually pay attention to how things work. I see how the dispatchers mess up the routing, and I know exactly how to fix it. That's not a superpower, Doc, that's just good old-fashioned experience and elbow grease. 

Like, just last Thursday, I was explaining to the terminal manager—because he was trying to tell me my new route plan was too aggressive—I told him, "Look, buddy, I don't have a magic wand, I just know how to read a topographic map better than your computer program does." So, I don't think I'm on some divine mission or anything. I just think I'm the only one actually operating at a hundred percent right now while everyone else is sleepwalking through their shift. But no, I'm firmly planted in reality. I just happen to be moving through it a heck of a lot faster than the rest of them.

symptom_reasoning.S035: The patient displays inflated self-confidence and grandiosity, stating he could run the whole company and is the only one operating at a hundred percent.
symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly denies having special powers or being on a secret mission.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing or seeing things that aren't there.

turns.doctor_question: During these high-energy periods, have they ever gotten so severe that you were hospitalized or they seriously disrupted your work or home life?
turns.patient_response:
Hospitalized? Oh, lord, no. No, definitely not. I’ve never been in the hospital for anything except when I blew out my knee stepping off a loading dock back in '06. I'm not, you know, out of my mind or anything like that. 

But as for disrupting things... well, I guess if I'm being completely honest, it hasn't exactly been smooth sailing. Like I mentioned, I don't just drive, I do a lot of the driver-sales work too, right? So you're not just dropping a trailer and getting a signature; you're talking to the receiving managers, checking their inventory, trying to set up the next run or upsell a freight package. And lately... man, because my brain is just firing on all cylinders, jumping from the route plan to the fuel efficiency to the dock layout, I've been sort of dropping the ball on the basics. I’ll be on the phone with dispatch, or even right there standing in front of a client, and they’ll be giving me a gate code or a specific delivery window, and I’ll have to stop them and go, "Wait, hold on, run that by me again?" I'm having them repeat details that I absolutely should have tracked the first time. It's embarrassing, honestly. And a couple of my sales follow-ups—these are accounts I've been working with for years—they completely slipped through the cracks just because I was chasing way too many ideas at once. I get so wrapped up in reinventing the whole system that I forget to actually follow through on the day-to-day stuff. 

And then at home... man, that's the part that actually bothers me the most. Because in my head, I thought I was doing everybody this huge favor, right? Fixing the porch, tuning up the mower, getting all these projects done that have been sitting there forever. But I look around, and... I can see it. My wife, and my daughter too, they’ve just been walking on eggshells around me lately. My daughter usually jokes around with me the second I walk in the door, but now it's like they're both afraid to say the wrong thing, or they don't want to interrupt me when I'm in the middle of tearing through the garage because I'm so keyed up. I don't mean to be short with them, I really don't, but I'm just moving so fast. I'm supposed to be helping out around the house, being a good husband and taking the load off my wife, but I can tell I’m just adding strain. It's like my energy is just sucking all the air out of the room. So, yeah, no hospitals, but I guess... I guess it is messing things up a bit more than I wanted to admit.
